name: Next.js + TypeScript
description: Enforces Next.js 14+ and TypeScript best practices. Covers App Router conventions, type safety, performance patterns, and common pitfalls in production Next.js codebases.
author: Solon AI

rules.title: No explicit 'any' types
rules.description: Explicit 'any' types defeat the purpose of TypeScript. Use 'unknown' and narrow the type, or define a proper interface.

rules.title: All component props must be typed
rules.description: React components must have explicit prop type definitions using interfaces or type aliases. No implicit props.

examples.bad: export default function Card({ title, onClick }) {}
examples.good: interface CardProps { title: string; onClick: () => void; } export default function Card({ title, onClick }: CardProps) {}

rules.title: Prefer Server Components unless client interactivity is needed
rules.description: In the App Router, components are Server Components by default. Only add 'use client' when you need useState, useEffect, event listeners, or browser APIs. Unnecessarily marking components as client-side increases bundle size.

examples.bad:
'use client'; export default function StaticCard({ title }: { title: string }) { return
{title}
; }
examples.good:
export default function StaticCard({ title }: { title: string }) { return
{title}
; }

rules.title: Do not use useEffect for data fetching
rules.description: In Next.js App Router, fetch data in Server Components or use React Query / SWR in Client Components. useEffect-based fetching causes waterfall requests, flickering, and no caching.

examples.good: const data = await fetch('/api/data', { next: { revalidate: 60 } }).then(r => r.json());

rules.title: No console.log statements
rules.description: Remove console.log before merging. Use a structured logger or Next.js built-in logging. Console statements leak implementation details and degrade performance.

rules.title: Use next/image instead of
rules.description: Raw tags bypass Next.js image optimization (lazy loading, WebP conversion, size optimization). Always use the Image component from next/image.

examples.good: import Image from 'next/image'; <Image src='/hero.png' alt='Hero' width={800} height={400} />

rules.title: Use next/link instead of <a> for internal navigation
rules.description: Raw anchor tags cause full page reloads and bypass Next.js prefetching. Use the Link component for all internal routes.

rules.title: All async functions must handle errors
rules.description: Unhandled promise rejections crash the app silently in production. Wrap async calls in try/catch or use a result pattern.

examples.bad: async function getUser(id: string) { const user = await db.users.find(id); return user; }
examples.good: async function getUser(id: string) { try { const user = await db.users.find(id); return user; } catch (error) { logger.error({ error, id }, 'Failed to fetch user'); throw error; } }

rules.title: No hardcoded environment-specific values
rules.description: URLs, API keys, and environment-specific strings must come from environment variables. Hardcoded values break across environments and leak secrets.

rules.title: Route handlers must validate request input
rules.description: All Next.js API route handlers must validate and sanitize incoming request data using zod or equivalent before processing. Never trust raw request input.

examples.bad: export async function POST(req: Request) { const { email } = await req.json(); await createUser(email); }
examples.good: const schema = z.object({ email: z.string().email() }); export async function POST(req: Request) { const body = schema.parse(await req.json()); await createUser(body.email); }

rules.title: Async UI must have loading and error states
rules.description: Any component that fetches data or performs async operations must handle loading and error states explicitly. Missing states cause layout shifts and confusing UX.

examples.bad:
export default function UserList() { const { data } = useQuery('users', fetchUsers); return
{data?.map(u =>
{u.name}
)}
; }
examples.good:
export default function UserList() { const { data, isLoading, error } = useQuery('users', fetchUsers); if (isLoading) return ; if (error) return ; return
{data.map(u =>
{u.name}
)}
; }

rules.title: API routes must return correct HTTP status codes
rules.description: Return semantically correct status codes. 200 for success, 201 for created, 400 for bad input, 401 for unauthenticated, 403 for unauthorized, 404 for not found, 500 for server errors. Never return 200 with an error body.

examples.good: return NextResponse.json({ error: 'User not found' }, { status: 404 });
